Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 35, verse 38:

﴿Indeed, He is Knower of what is within the breasts.﴾

It is like a causal explanation: since He knows what is in the breasts, which is the most hidden of things, He knows every unseen thing in the world. Dhat al-sudur (what is within the breasts) means their concealed contents. Here dhu is in its feminine form (dhat), as in the saying of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him: "Dhu batni Kharija jariyah" [Narrated in al-Muwatta' from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah, from Aisha: "Abu Bakr had given me the produce of twenty wasqs of date-palms… the hadith," and in it: "It is only Asma'. Which of the others is it?" He said: "Dhu batni bint Kharija; I think it is a girl," and she gave birth to a girl. Part of this has already been mentioned in the chapter on the Isra'.] And the line of verse:

"Wa-nawalatuhu min rusli kawma'a jaldatan... wa-aghdaytu 'anhu al-tarfa hatta tadallaʿa
Idha qala qaddani qultu billahi halfatan... litughnanna 'anni dha inaʾika ajma'a"

It belongs to Huraith ibn Attab al-Ta'i. Al-rusl (with a kasra) is thin milk; al-kawma'a is the plump (camel); al-jaldah is the firm one; al-ighda' is lowering and closing the eyes; al-tadallu' is the belly becoming full until both flanks and ribs rise. He lowered his gaze from the guest so that the guest would not feel ashamed when he said, "Qaddani" (enough for me of drinking), and he replied, "By Allah." It is also narrated as "qala billah," as if he expressed himself in the third person by way of indirect speech.

It is also narrated as: "Idha qulta qaddani qala," on the basis that the poet is the guest, though this is not the case. "Halfatan" is in the accusative, serving as an oath preceding it, meaning: "I swear by Allah an oath." "Litughnā" is the answer to the oath, and its final vowel is open because it is connected, in estimation, to the light emphatic nun: meaning, "you shall keep me away from myself." Tha'lab narrated it as "litughnanna" with the heavy emphatic nun, meaning "you shall indeed remove yourself far from me." According to the well-known dialect, it should have been "litughninna," but its ya' was dropped after the kasra, in the dialect of Fazarah. It is also narrated as "litughnā" with a kasra on the lam, as a causal particle, meaning: "drink, so that the owner of your vessel, which is the milk, may be sufficient for me." He attributed it to the vessel because it is in it, and he attributed the vessel to the guest's pronoun because it is in his hand, and he disowned its attribution to himself as a sign of generosity. "Ajma'a" is an emphasis on the milk, meaning: do not return anything to what is in the vessel; rather, drink all of it.

The meaning is: what is in her womb of the fetus, and what is in your vessel of drink, because the fetus and the drink accompany the womb and the vessel. Do you not see their saying: "Ma'aha hamlun" (she has a fetus with her)? Likewise, the concealed contents accompany the breasts, and they are with them.

Dhu is laid down to signify the meaning of companionship.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 35, verse 39:

It is said of the one who is appointed as a successor: khalifah (ﺧﻠﻴﻔﺔ) and khalif (ﺧﻠﻴﻒ). The plural of khalifah is khala'if, and the plural of khalif is khulafa'. The meaning is:

That He made you His successors (khulafa'uhu) on His earth, having granted you possession of the keys of disposal over it and given you authority over what is in it, and having permitted you its benefits, so that you may thank Him through monotheism and obedience. ﴿So whoever among you disbelieves, the harm of his disbelief falls back upon him﴾ and whoever scorns (ghamata) such a lofty blessing [[His saying "wa ghamata mithla hadhihi al-ni'mah al-sunniyyah" means: and belittles it. (A)]], the harm of his disbelief returns upon him, which is the loathing of Allah, beyond which there is no further disgrace, humiliation and loss in the Hereafter, after which no loss remains. Al-maqt means intense hatred. From this comes the saying about one who marries his father's wife: "maqti" (a hateful one), because he is loathed in every heart. This address is to mankind. It has also been said that it is an address to those to whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent. ﴿He made you a community that succeeded those before it﴾, and you saw and witnessed among those who passed away what you should take as a lesson. So whoever among you disbelieves, upon him is the penalty of his disbelief: the loathing of Allah and the loss of the Hereafter, just as that has been the judgment upon those before you.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 35, verse 40:

"Show me" (أَرُونِي) is a substitute (badal) for "Have you considered" (أرأيتم), because the meaning is: "Have you considered? Inform me." It is as if he said: "Inform me about these partners, and about what they deserved by which they were made divinities and partners. Show me what part of the parts of the earth they independently created apart from God, or whether they have a share with God in the creation of the heavens. Or do they have a Book from God that speaks that they are His partners, so that they stand upon proof and evidence from that Book?"

Or the pronoun in ﴿آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ (We have given them) may refer to the polytheists, like His saying, ﴿Or have We sent down to them an authority?﴾ ﴿Or have We given them a Book before this?﴾ ﴿But the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion﴾, that is, the leaders promise the followers nothing but delusion, which is their saying: ﴿These are our intercessors with God.﴾ And it is read: "bayyinat" (clear proofs).

**﴿That they should not cease﴾**: meaning, lest they cease. Or, He prevents them from ceasing, since *al-imsak* (holding back) is a form of prevention.

﴿Indeed, He is Forbearing, Forgiving﴾: not hastening punishment, in that He holds them back, though they were worthy of collapsing entirely because of the magnitude of the word of shirk, as He says: ﴿The heavens are almost splitting apart from it, and the earth is cleaved asunder﴾.

It was read (*qurri'a*, a variant reading): *wa-lau zalana* (and if they had ceased), and *wa-in amsakahuma* (and if He held them).

The answer to the oath in *wa-la'in zalatā* stands in place of the two answers (of the conditional and the oath). The *min* in *al-ūlā* is extra, for emphasis of the negation, and the second *min* is for the beginning. *Min ba'dihi*: after His holding them.

From Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said to a man who came from al-Sham: "Whom did you meet there?" He said: "Ka'b." He said: "And what did you hear him say?" He said: "I heard him say: 'Indeed the heavens are upon the shoulder of an angel.'" He said: "Ka'b lied. Did he not leave his Judaism after [[I have not found it. al-Tabari narrated, through the transmission of Abu Wa'il, who said: A man came to 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: "Where have you come from?" He said: "From al-Sham," and he mentioned something similar, except that he did not say "did he not leave his Judaism."]]" Then he recited this verse.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 35, verse 42–44:

It reached Quraysh before the mission of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that the People of the Book had denied their messengers, so they said: "May God curse the Jews and the Christians! Messengers came to them and they denied them. By God, if a messenger comes to us, we will surely be more guided than any one of the (other) nations." Then when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was sent, they denied him.

In ﴿إِحْدَى الْأُمَمِ﴾ (one of the nations) there are two interpretations. The first: "from among some of the nations," meaning one nation among the nations, from among the Jews, the Christians, and others.

The second: "from the nation that is called 'one of the nations'," preferring it over others in guidance and uprightness.

﴿مَا زَادَهُمْ﴾ (it increased them not) is a metaphorical attribution (isnad majazi), because it is in fact the cause of their increasing themselves in ﴿نُفُورًا﴾ (aversion) from the truth and distance from it, like His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿فَزَادَتْهُمْ رِجْسًا إِلَىٰ رِجْسِهِمْ﴾ (so it added to them uncleanness upon their uncleanness).

﴿اسْتِكْبَارًا﴾ (arrogance) is a substitute (badal) for ﴿نُفُورًا﴾. Or it is an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu), meaning: "They increased only in aversion, out of arrogance and haughtiness ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ (in the land)." Or it is a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: arrogant and scheming against the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the believers.

It is permissible for ﴿وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ﴾ (and evil scheming) to be conjoined (ma'tuf) upon ﴿نُفُورًا﴾.

If you say: what is the reason for His saying ﴿وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ﴾? I say: its origin is: "and that they schemed the evil," i.e., the evil scheming; then "and schemers the evil"; then "and scheming the evil." The evidence for this is His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَلَا يَحِيقُ الْمَكْرُ السَّيِّئُ إِلَّا بِأَهْلِهِ﴾ (and evil scheming does not encompass anyone except its own people).

The meaning of ﴿يَحِيقُ﴾ (encompass) is: it surrounds and descends.

It was recited: ﴿وَلَا يَحِيقُ الْمَكْرُ السَّيِّئُ﴾, i.e., "the evil scheming does not encompass" (the one who schemes); and ﴿وَلَقَدْ حَاقَ بِهِمْ﴾ (it did indeed encompass them) at the day of Badr.

From the Prophet (ﷺ): "Do not scheme, and do not assist a schemer, for God, Exalted is He, says: ﴿وَلَا يَحِيقُ الْمَكْرُ السَّيِّئُ إِلَّا بِأَهْلِهِ﴾ (and evil scheming does not encompass anyone except its own people). Do not transgress, and do not assist a transgressor; God, Exalted is He, says: ﴿إِنَّمَا بَغْيُكُم عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِكُم﴾ (your transgression is only against yourselves)." [Narrated by Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd. It has been mentioned earlier at the beginning of Yunus.]

And Ka'b said to Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: "I read in the Torah: whoever digs a pit (maghwah) falls into it." He said: "I found that in the Book of God," and he recited the verse.

Among the proverbs of the Arabs: "Whoever digs a pit for his brother falls into it headfirst."

Hamza recited ﴿وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ﴾ with the hamza silent (sukun), because of his finding the vowels heavy alongside the ya' and the hamza; perhaps he elided the vowel and thought it was a sukun, or paused briefly, then began ﴿وَلَا يَحِيقُ﴾.

Ibn Mas'ud recited: ﴿وَمَكْرًا سَيِّئًا﴾.

﴿سُنَّتَ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ (the way of the former peoples) refers to sending down punishment upon those among the nations before them who denied their messengers. Their awaiting it is described as their expectation of it, and it is shown that His custom, which is the vengeance upon those who deny the messengers, is a custom that He does not change or alter, i.e., He does not modify it, and that it is a matter that will certainly come to pass. He cited as evidence what they witnessed in their travels and trade caravans to Syria, Iraq and Yemen: the traces of those who passed away and the signs of their destruction and ruin.

﴿لِيُعْجِزَهُ﴾ (so as to elude Him) means: to outrun Him and escape Him.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 35, verse 45:

Because of what they earned: because of what they committed of their sins. ﴿On its back﴾: on the surface of the earth. ﴿Not a creature﴾: no living being (nasamah) that crawls upon it. He means the children of Adam. It is also said: He would leave none of the children of Adam or the other beasts of every kind because of the evil of their sins.

It is related from Ibn Mas'ud: "The dung beetle (ja'al) nearly is punished in its hole for the sin of the son of Adam," [Al-Hakim transmitted it, and it has already been mentioned in al-Nahl], then he recited this verse. And from Anas:

"Indeed the lizard (dabb) dies of hunger in its hole for the sin of the son of Adam." [I have not found it from Anas; it has already been mentioned in al-Nahl from Abu Hurayrah, and the author attributed it there correctly.]

It is also said: He would hold back the rain, so every living thing would perish. ﴿Until a term appointed﴾: until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Indeed He is ever, of His servants, All-Seeing﴾: a warning of recompense.

From the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surah al-Mala'ikah, the eight gates of Paradise will call him: enter by whichever gate you wish."
